sessions.title: What is antibody
sessions.last_message_preview: An antibody is a Y-shaped immune protein made by B cells that specifically recognizes and binds a target, usually part of a virus, bacterium, toxin, or other foreign substance called an antigen. Antibodies help protect the body by neutralizing threats, blocking their activity, or marking them for destruction by other immune cells.

sessions.title: Help me figure out where to buy this selected lab item.
sessions.last_message_preview:
Assuming this is for routine cloning ligation, buy `T4 DNA ligase` from NEB first. The best default is `NEB T4 DNA Ligase` because it is a standard cloning reagent, includes 10X buffer, and is easy to source direct or through common distributors.

Current US options I verified on May 8, 2026:
- `NEB M0202S` (20,000 U, 400,000 U/mL) or `M0202T` (20,000 U, 2,000,000 U/mL). NEB lists both at `$71`; Fisher also carries `M0202S`.
- `Thermo Scientific EL0011` (1,000 Weiss units, 5 U/µL). Available direct from Thermo and through Fisher; Thermo lists `$262.65` direct.
- `QIAGEN L6030-HC-L` if you specifically want a high-concentration rapid/blunt-end or NGS-oriented format; QIAGEN lists it at `$813`.

Recommendation: choose `NEB M0202S` for normal ligations, or `NEB M0202T` if you want the same total units in a smaller volume or expect more blunt-end work. If your lab already buys through a distributor, Fisher carries both NEB and Thermo options.

sessions.last_message_preview: Sanger sequencing is a DNA sequencing method that determines the order of bases in a DNA strand by copying the DNA and occasionally inserting special chain-terminating nucleotides. Those terminated fragments are separated by size, and the final base on each fragment reveals the DNA sequence. It is highly accurate and is commonly used for sequencing short DNA regions, validating plasmids, and confirming variants, though it is lower-throughput than next-generation sequencing.

sessions.title: What is the difference between CD4+ and CD8+ cells?
sessions.last_message_preview: CD4+ cells are helper T cells that coordinate immune responses by activating other immune cells, whereas CD8+ cells are cytotoxic T cells that directly kill infected or abnormal cells.
